t.E172.agn: In 1980 JECFA had set the ADI at 0–0.5 mg/kg body weight/day. In 2015 EFSA reported that red and black iron oxide gave positive results in genotoxicity tests in cell experiments, that the available data were not sufficient to assess this, and that the safety of E 172 could not be assessed because sufficient biological and toxicological data were lacking.
t.E172.body: Iron absorption from iron oxides is low.
t.E172.eff.0.t: EFSA could not assess its safety because sufficient biological and toxicological data were lacking
t.E172.found.0: In the EU, as a Group II colour in many foods at quantum satis: flavoured fermented milk products and cheeses, confectionery and chewing gum, breakfast cereals, fine bakery wares, sauces, mustard and seasonings, flavoured drinks, cider and fruit wines, snacks
t.E172.found.1: Markings on citrus, melon and pomegranate peel (for contrast)
t.E172.found.2: Fish and crustacean pastes, smoked fish
t.E172.regx.0: Re-evaluated; safety could not be assessed because of insufficient data.
t.E172.regx.1: Group II colour: quantum satis in the authorised food categories.
t.E172.summary: Oxides and hydroxides of iron; give a yellow, red or black colour. Used in confectionery coatings and medicine tablets.
t.E172.what: A colour giving earthy tones, made up of yellow, red and black iron oxides and hydroxides.
